candidates.title: Compare supplier confirmations with purchase orders

demandEvidence.chore: Manually compare supplier confirmation line items with the purchase order across SKU, quantity, price, and delivery date.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: When a supplier confirmation contains dozens of line items, manually comparing every SKU, quantity, price, and delivery date against the original Purchase Order becomes time-consuming.

ease.reason: A beginner can compare supplied sample rows, but the discussion contains no tool setup evidence.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops managing supplier orders might pay for comparison preparation; no payment evidence is given.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test could compare synthetic rows and flag differences; document intake and matching accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed matcher can flag differences, but a person must check source data and every mismatch; no implementation reference is supplied.

evidence.reason: The primary post names the manual comparison and fields, but provides no frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete task assessed with a synthetic row comparison; the evidence is unchanged from prior assessments, and the provisional mean is below 6. The proposed ecommerce buyer also overlaps the online-retailer customer in recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6.

candidates.title: Prepare customer order status updates

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare customer-facing order status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: A student could draft from operator-supplied sample status fields, but no supplied reference documents the workflow.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small ecommerce operators might pay for clearer update preparation; the discussion proves no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test could draft one update from fictional order rows; live store access and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed draft step is repeatable, but a person must resolve missing or changing data and approve each message.

evidence.reason: The primary post states the status-update problem and changing or incomplete inputs, but gives no frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: The request supports a bounded draft-from-sample-data experiment, but there is no implementation reference and the provisional mean is below the threshold.

candidates.title: Notify a restaurant when an order arrives

demandEvidence.chore: Notify the operator when a new restaurant website order arrives.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A beginner could mock a new-order event and alert, but no supplied reference documents the connection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small restaurant operators might pay for order alert setup; this request establishes no payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can turn sample order events into alerts; live ordering access and delivery need validation.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-alert loop is repeatable, but an operator must verify orders and handle missed alerts.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly names an automated restaurant order notification system, but provides little workflow detail or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete request assessed as a mock event-to-alert experiment; the same unchanged evidence was previously assessed below threshold, and no implementation reference is supplied.
